headline: Report: Nikita Kucherov Requests Trade From Tampa Bay Lightning
take:
The Hockey News reports that reigning Hart Trophy winner Nikita Kucherov has requested a trade from the Lightning. The Athletic notes he assisted on Tampa Bay's first three goals in a 5-4 shootout loss to Nashville on Saturday, and Daily Faceoff posted that his agent, Dan Milstein, said "It's time to move on."

Whatever the dispute, Kucherov is still driving the team. So far this season he has 20 points in 14 games, and Tampa Bay controls 59% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) with him on the ice at five-on-five. The Lightning's share of those chances is also about 5 percentage points better with him playing, which is a big gap for a team already at 55.7% overall. His four goals sit just under his own expected total of 4.42, so there's no luck inflating his line. This is real production, and the Lightning's 9-3-2 record looks sturdy, even with goaltending that has cost them 2.9 goals against what the shots called for.

That's the problem for any suitor and for Tampa Bay: we'd be moving a player whose impact shows up in the underlying numbers, not just the scoring column.
